senses.definition: Body material made of a group of cells and nearby material working together.
senses.example: Muscle tissue can pull as it shortens.

senses.definition: A quick response the body makes without you having to decide first.
senses.example: Pulling away quickly from a sharp point can be a reflex.

senses.definition: A beat you can feel when pressure from the heart moves through an artery.
senses.example: A heartbeat starts the pressure change you notice as a pulse.

senses.definition: One of the first teeth that grow in, most often later replaced with another tooth.
senses.example: A baby tooth came loose and moved a little.

senses.definition: A tooth in the set most people keep after losing their first teeth.
senses.example: My first permanent tooth appeared as my jaw grew.

senses.definition: A front tooth with a sharp edge used for cutting into food.
senses.example: An incisor cut off a small piece of apple.

senses.definition: A large tooth farther back in the mouth, used to crush and grind food.
senses.example: This molar helps me chew pieces of bread.

senses.definition: A cell near the back of the eye that responds well to weak light.
senses.example: Rod cells help me see the ground in very dim light.

senses.definition: A cell in the eye that helps you see colors and details in enough light.
senses.example: Different cone cells can respond more strongly to different colors of light.

senses.definition: The ability to notice how far away things are or which objects are nearer than others.
senses.example: Depth perception helps me tell which branch is closer.

senses.definition: A place that keeps a copy of information so a computer may use it again quickly.
senses.example: The browser could read the image from its cache.

senses.definition: Words that describe what matters about an image for someone who cannot see it.
senses.example: Alt text describes what the button with a picture of a house does.

senses.definition: Written words that help explain a picture or tell what you would hear in a video.
senses.example: A caption told the viewer that a phone was ringing.

senses.definition: Software that can turn computer text and controls into spoken words or braille.
senses.example: The screen reader spoke the name of the button.

senses.definition: A square pattern of small light and dark areas made to be read as information by a device.
senses.example: The QR code held the address of a web page.

senses.definition: A computer table where you can organize values and use calculations based on them.
senses.example: My spreadsheet added all the numbers in the last column.

senses.definition: An organized set of information that a program can search and use.
senses.example: We searched a database for books written by the same person.

senses.definition: Information that describes a file or other piece of information.
senses.example: A photo’s metadata can describe when the picture was made.
